content.overview: Section 7 incorporation, followed by the certificate under s. 7, brings the company into existence; s. 9 gives it succession and a common seal where used, and power to hold property and sue.
content.glance: Section 7 incorporation, followed by the certificate under s. 7, brings the company into existence; s. 9 gives it succession and a common seal where used, and power to hold property and sue.
content.study: Formation needs the minimum members in s. 3 and filing of memorandum, articles, declarations, address and particulars of first directors. The Registrar registers and issues the certificate, which is conclusive evidence that the Act has been complied with. Pre-incorporation contracts do not bind the company unless novated after incorporation; promoters remain personally liable. Commencement of business is now the declaration route inserted as s. 10A; s. 11 was omitted.

caseLaw.name: Salomon v A Salomon & Co Ltd
caseLaw.point: Incorporation creates a separate legal person. The certificate of incorporation is conclusive evidence that the requirements of the Act have been complied with, as section 7 now provides.
